name: Reddish crimson
lede: Reddish crimson is the ColorHub library's English gloss for Nakabeni, a Japanese dye name meaning a medium crimson.

sections.title: A gloss for Nakabeni
sections.body:
The library files this hex under the Japanese traditional-color name *Nakabeni* (中紅), whose kanji read literally as "medium crimson" and name a mid-strength shade of the safflower-dyed crimson family [1]. "Reddish crimson" is the plain-English gloss chosen so the color reads without the Japanese word [1]. The hex #C93756 is a screen approximation; no source here gives a dye recipe or date for this specific shade [1].

Its nearest library look-alike is [[brick-red]], about 2.9 units away in LCH space [1]. The parent hue, [[crimson]], names the whole family this shade belongs to [1].

Other close matches in the library include [[lipstick]], a more vivid red, and [[french-raspberry]], almost the same color [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In the ColorHub painting archive this hue appears in 4 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, including a 1925 portrait by Pierre Bonnard and two Indian paintings from around 1890 [2]. The match rate is well under one percent, so these are a handful of close calls rather than a pattern [2].
